NASB.1: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel, who was named Belteshazzar; and the message was true and [one of] great conflict, but he understood the message and had an understanding of the vision.
NASB.2: In those days, I, Daniel, had been mourning for three entire weeks.
NASB.3: I did not eat any tasty food, nor did meat or wine enter my mouth, nor did I use any ointment at all until the entire three weeks were completed.
NASB.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while I was by the bank of the great river, that is, the Tigris,
NASB.5: I lifted my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a certain man dressed in linen, whose waist was girded with [a belt of] pure gold of Uphaz.
NASB.6: His body also [was] like beryl, his face had the appearance of lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and feet like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a tumult.
NASB.7: Now I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, while the men who were with me did not see the vision; nevertheless, a great dread fell on them, and they ran away to hide themselves.
NASB.8: So I was left alone and saw this great vision; yet no strength was left in me, for my natural color turned to a deathly pallor, and I retained no strength.
NASB.9: But I heard the sound of his words; and as soon as I heard the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face to the ground.
NASB.10: Then behold, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
NASB.11: He said to me, 'O Daniel, man of high esteem, understand the words that I am about to tell you and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you.' And when he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling.
NASB.12: Then he said to me, 'Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart on understanding [this] and on humbling yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to your words.
NASB.13: 'But the prince of the kingdom of Persia was withstanding me for twenty-one days; then behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
NASB.14: 'Now I have come to give you an understanding of what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision pertains to the days yet [future].'
NASB.15: When he had spoken to me according to these words, I turned my face toward the ground and became speechless.
NASB.16: And behold, one who resembled a human being was touching my lips; then I opened my mouth and spoke and said to him who was standing before me, 'O my lord, as a result of the vision anguish has come upon me, and I have retained no strength.
NASB.17: 'For how can such a servant of my lord talk with such as my lord? As for me, there remains just now no strength in me, nor has any breath been left in me.'
NASB.18: Then [this] one with human appearance touched me again and strengthened me.
NASB.19: He said, 'O man of high esteem, do not be afraid. Peace be with you; take courage and be courageous!' Now as soon as he spoke to me, I received strength and said, 'May my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.'
NASB.20: Then he said, 'Do you understand why I came to you? But I shall now return to fight against the prince of Persia; so I am going forth, and behold, the prince of Greece is about to come.
NASB.21: 'However, I will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth. Yet there is no one who stands firmly with me against these [forces] except Michael your prince.

ESV.1: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a word was revealed to Daniel, who was named Belteshazzar. And the word was true, and it was a great conflict.  And he understood the word and had understanding of the vision.
ESV.2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks.
ESV.3: I ate no delicacies, no meat or wine entered my mouth, nor did I anoint myself at all, for the full three weeks.
ESV.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river (that is, the Tigris)
ESV.5: I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a man clothed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.
ESV.6: His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
ESV.7: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, for the men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.
ESV.8: So I was left alone and saw this great vision, and no strength was left in me. My radiant appearance was fearfully changed,  and I retained no strength.
ESV.9: Then I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard the sound of his words, I fell on my face in deep sleep with my face to the ground.
ESV.10: And behold, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
ESV.11: And he said to me, “O Daniel, man greatly loved, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright, for now I have been sent to you.” And when he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling.
ESV.12: Then he said to me, “Fear not, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and humbled yourself before your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words.
ESV.13: The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days, but Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I was left there with the kings of Persia,
ESV.14: and came to make you understand what is to happen to your people in the latter days. For the vision is for days yet to come.”
ESV.15: When he had spoken to me according to these words, I turned my face toward the ground and was mute.
ESV.16: And behold, one in the likeness of the children of man touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth and spoke. I said to him who stood before me, “O my lord, by reason of the vision pains have come upon me, and I retain no strength.
ESV.17: How can my lord's servant talk with my lord? For now no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me.”
ESV.18: Again one having the appearance of a man touched me and strengthened me.
ESV.19: And he said, “O man greatly loved, fear not, peace be with you; be strong and of good courage.” And as he spoke to me, I was strengthened and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”
ESV.20: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? But now I will return to fight against the prince of Persia; and when I go out, behold, the prince of Greece will come.
ESV.21: But I will tell you what is inscribed in the book of truth: there is none who contends by my side against these except Michael, your prince.

NKJV.19: And he said, “O man greatly beloved, fear not! Peace be to you; be strong, yes, be strong!” So when he spoke to me I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”

WEB.1: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, even a great warfare: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
WEB.2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks.
WEB.3: I ate no pleasant bread, neither came meat nor wine into my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, until three whole weeks were fulfilled.
WEB.4: In the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel,
WEB.5: I lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, a man clothed in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold of Uphaz:
WEB.6: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
WEB.7: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; for the men who were with me didn’t see the vision; but a great quaking fell on them, and they fled to hide themselves.
WEB.8: So I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me; for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.
WEB.9: Yet heard I the voice of his words; and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I fallen into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.
WEB.10: Behold, a hand touched me, which set me on my knees and on the palms of my hands.
WEB.11: He said to me, Daniel, you man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright; for am I now sent to you. When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling.
WEB.12: Then he said to me, Don’t be afraid, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard: and I have come for your words’ sake.
WEB.13: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; but, behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me: and I remained there with the kings of Persia.
WEB.14: Now I have come to make you understand what shall happen to your people in the latter days; for the vision is yet for many days:
WEB.15: and when he had spoken to me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground, and was mute.
WEB.16: Behold, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spoke and said to him who stood before me, my lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows are turned on me, and I retain no strength.
WEB.17: For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, immediately there remained no strength in me, neither was there breath left in me.
WEB.18: Then there touched me again one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me.
WEB.19: He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid: peace be to you, be strong, yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak; for you have strengthened me.”
WEB.20: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, behold, the prince of Greece shall come.
WEB.21: But I will tell you that which is inscribed in the writing of truth: and there is no one who holds with me against these, but Michael your prince.”

AMP.1: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel, who was named Belteshazzar; and the message was true and it referred to great conflict (warfare, misery). And he understood the message and had an understanding of the vision.
AMP.2: In those days I, Daniel, had been mourning for three entire weeks.
AMP.3: I ate no tasty food, nor did any meat or wine enter my mouth; and I did not anoint (refresh, groom) myself at all for the full three weeks.
AMP.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was on the bank of the great river Hiddekel [which is the Tigris],
AMP.5: I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a certain man dressed in linen, whose loins were girded with [a belt of] pure gold of Uphaz.
AMP.6: His body also was like beryl [with a golden luster], his face had the appearance of lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and his feet like the gleam of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words was like the noise of a multitude [of people or the roaring of the sea].
AMP.7: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision [of this heavenly being], for the men who were with me did not see the vision; nevertheless, a great panic overwhelmed them, so they ran away to hide themselves.
AMP.8: So I was left alone and saw this great vision; yet no strength was left in me, for my normal appearance turned to a deathly pale, and I grew weak and faint [with fright].
AMP.9: Then I heard the sound of his words; and when I heard the sound of his words, I fell on my face in a deep sleep, with my face toward the ground.
AMP.10: Then behold, a hand touched me and set me unsteadily on my hands and knees.
AMP.11: So he said to me, "O Daniel, you highly regarded and greatly beloved man, understand the words that I am about to say to you and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you." And while he was saying this word to me, I stood up trembling.
AMP.12: Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart on understanding this and on humbling yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to your words.
AMP.13: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia was standing in opposition to me for twenty-one days. Then, behold, Michael, one of the chief [of the celestial] princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
AMP.14: Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision is in regard to the days yet to come."
AMP.15: When he had spoken to me according to these words, I turned my face toward the ground and was speechless.
AMP.16: And behold, one who resembled the sons of men touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth and spoke and said to him who was standing before me, "O my lord, because of the vision anguish has come upon me, and I have retained no strength.
AMP.17: For how can such a [weakened] servant of my lord talk with such [a being] as my lord? For now there remains no strength in me, nor has any breath been left in me."
AMP.18: Then the one (Gabriel) whose appearance was like that of a man touched me again, and he strengthened me.
AMP.19: He said, "O man, highly regarded and greatly beloved, do not be afraid. Peace be to you; take courage and be strong." Now when he had spoken to me, I was strengthened and said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
AMP.20: Then he said, "Do you understand [fully] why I came to you? Now I shall return to fight against the [hostile] prince of Persia; and when I have gone, behold, the prince of Greece is about to come.
AMP.21: But I (Gabriel) will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth. There is no one who stands firmly with me and strengthens himself against these [hostile spirit forces] except Michael, your prince [the guardian of your nation].

CSB17.3: I didn’t eat any rich food, <sup>ⓚ</sup> no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I didn’t put any oil on my body until the three weeks were over.

NLT.1: In the third year of the reign of King Cyrus of Persia, Daniel (also known as Belteshazzar) had another vision. He understood that the vision concerned events certain to happen in the future — times of war and great hardship.
NLT.2: When this vision came to me, I, Daniel, had been in mourning for three whole weeks.
NLT.3: All that time I had eaten no rich food. No meat or wine crossed my lips, and I used no fragrant lotions until those three weeks had passed.
NLT.4: On April 23, as I was standing on the bank of the great Tigris River,
NLT.5: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen clothing, with a belt of pure gold around his waist.
NLT.6: His body looked like a precious gem. His face flashed like lightning, and his eyes flamed like torches. His arms and feet shone like polished bronze, and his voice roared like a vast multitude of people.
NLT.7: Only I, Daniel, saw this vision. The men with me saw nothing, but they were suddenly terrified and ran away to hide.
NLT.8: So I was left there all alone to see this amazing vision. My strength left me, my face grew deathly pale, and I felt very weak.
NLT.9: Then I heard the man speak, and when I heard the sound of his voice, I fainted and lay there with my face to the ground.
NLT.10: Just then a hand touched me and lifted me, still trembling, to my hands and knees.
NLT.11: And the man said to me, “Daniel, you are very precious to God, so listen carefully to what I have to say to you. Stand up, for I have been sent to you.” When he said this to me, I stood up, still trembling.
NLT.12: Then he said, “Don’t be afraid, Daniel. Since the first day you began to pray for understanding and to humble yourself before your God, your request has been heard in heaven. I have come in answer to your prayer.
NLT.13: But for twenty-one days the spirit prince of the kingdom of Persia blocked my way. Then Michael, one of the archangels, came to help me, and I left him there with the spirit prince of the kingdom of Persia.
NLT.14: Now I am here to explain what will happen to your people in the future, for this vision concerns a time yet to come.”
NLT.15: While he was speaking to me, I looked down at the ground, unable to say a word.
NLT.16: Then the one who looked like a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing in front of me, “I am filled with anguish because of the vision I have seen, my lord, and I am very weak.
NLT.17: How can someone like me, your servant, talk to you, my lord? My strength is gone, and I can hardly breathe.”
NLT.18: Then the one who looked like a man touched me again, and I felt my strength returning.
NLT.19: “Don’t be afraid,” he said, “for you are very precious to God. Peace! Be encouraged! Be strong!” As he spoke these words to me, I suddenly felt stronger and said to him, “Please speak to me, my lord, for you have strengthened me.”
NLT.20: He replied, “Do you know why I have come? Soon I must return to fight against the spirit prince of the kingdom of Persia, and after that the spirit prince of the kingdom of Greece will come.
NLT.21: Meanwhile, I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. (No one helps me against these spirit princes except Michael, your spirit prince.

NIV.1:
Daniel’s Vision of a Man
In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a revelation was given to Daniel (who was called Belteshazzar). Its message was true and it concerned a great war. The understanding of the message came to him in a vision.
NIV.2: At that time I, Daniel, mourned for three weeks.
NIV.3: I ate no choice food; no meat or wine touched my lips; and I used no lotions at all until the three weeks were over.
NIV.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
NIV.5: I looked up and there before me was a man dressed in linen, with a belt of the finest gold around his waist.
NIV.6: His body was like chrysolite, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.
NIV.7: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but such terror overwhelmed them that they fled and hid themselves.
NIV.8: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision; I had no strength left, my face turned deathly pale and I was helpless.
NIV.9: Then I heard him speaking, and as I listened to him, I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground.
NIV.10: A hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
NIV.11: He said, “Daniel, you who are highly esteemed, consider carefully the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have now been sent to you.” And when he said this to me, I stood up trembling.
NIV.12: Then he continued, “Do not be afraid, Daniel. Since the first day that you set your mind to gain understanding and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
NIV.13: But the prince of the Persian kingdom resisted me twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, because I was detained there with the king of Persia.
NIV.14: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the future, for the vision concerns a time yet to come.”
NIV.15: While he was saying this to me, I bowed with my face toward the ground and was speechless.
NIV.16: Then one who looked like a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing before me, “I am overcome with anguish because of the vision, my lord, and I am helpless.
NIV.17: How can I, your servant, talk with you, my lord? My strength is gone and I can hardly breathe.”
NIV.18: Again the one who looked like a man touched me and gave me strength.
NIV.19:
“Do not be afraid, O man highly esteemed,” he said. “Peace! Be strong now; be strong.”
When he spoke to me, I was strengthened and said, “Speak, my lord, since you have given me strength.”
NIV.20: So he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Soon I will return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go, the prince of Greece will come;
NIV.21: but first I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. (No one supports me against them except Michael, your prince.

NET.1: In the third year of King Cyrus of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel (who was also called Belteshazzar). This message was true and concerned a great war. He understood the message and gained insight by the vision.
NET.2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three whole weeks.
NET.3: I ate no choice food; no meat or wine came to my lips, nor did I anoint myself with oil until the end of those three weeks.
NET.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month I was beside the great river, the Tigris.
NET.5: I looked up and saw a man clothed in linen; around his waist was a belt made of gold from Upaz.
NET.6: His body resembled yellow jasper, and his face had an appearance like lightning. His eyes were like blazing torches; his arms and feet had the gleam of polished bronze. His voice thundered forth like the sound of a large crowd.
NET.7: Only I, Daniel, saw the vision; the men who were with me did not see it. On the contrary, they were overcome with fright and ran away to hide.
NET.8: I alone was left to see this great vision. My strength drained from me, and my vigor disappeared; I was without energy.
NET.9: I listened to his voice, and as I did so I fell into a trance-like sleep with my face to the ground.
NET.10: Then a hand touched me and set me on my hands and knees.
NET.11: He said to me, “Daniel, you are of great value. Understand the words that I am about to speak to you. So stand up, for I have now been sent to you.” When he said this to me, I stood up shaking.
NET.12: Then he said to me, “Don’t be afraid, Daniel, for from the very first day you applied your mind to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come in response to your words.
NET.13: However, the prince of the kingdom of Persia was opposing me for twenty-one days. But Michael, one of the leading princes, came to help me, because I was left there with the kings of Persia.
NET.14: Now I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision pertains to future days.”
NET.15: While he was saying this to me, I was flat on the ground and unable to speak.
NET.16: Then one who appeared to be a human being was touching my lips. I opened my mouth and started to speak, saying to the one who was standing before me, “Sir, due to the vision, anxiety has gripped me and I have no strength.
NET.17: How, sir, am I able to speak with you? My strength is gone, and I am breathless.”
NET.18: Then the one who appeared to be a human being touched me again and strengthened me.
NET.19: He said to me, “Don’t be afraid, you who are valued. Peace be to you! Be strong! Be really strong!” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened. I said, “Sir, you may speak now, for you have given me strength.”
NET.20: He said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I am about to return to engage in battle with the prince of Persia. When I go, the prince of Greece is coming.
NET.21: However, I will first tell you what is written in a dependable book. (There is no one who strengthens me against these princes, except Michael your prince.
